Consider the collection of point masses above, where the $x$-coordinates are measured in meters. What is the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass for this system?
worked_solution:
The center of mass, denoted $\overset{―}{x},$ of a collection of point masses ${m}_{1},{m}_{2},…,{m}_{n}$ located at ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ along the $x$-axis is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}$ is the total mass of the system,

- ${M}_{O}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}{x}_{i}$ is the total moment of the system about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =2, & \,{m}_{2} & =3, & \,{m}_{3} & =1, & \,{m}_{4} & =5, \\ {x}_{1} & =1, & \,{x}_{2} & =3, & \,{x}_{3} & =5, & \,{x}_{4} & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the total mass of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i} \\  & ={m}_{1}+{m}_{2}+{m}_{3}+{m}_{4} \\  & =2+3+1+5 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

and the total moment of the system about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & ={m}_{1}{x}_{1}+{m}_{2}{x}_{2}+{m}_{3}{x}_{3}+{m}_{4}{x}_{4} \\  & =2\cdot 1+3\cdot 3+1\cdot 5+5\cdot 6 \\  & =2+9+5+30 \\  & =46.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{46}{11}.
$$
